Hi Mike / James,

Thanks again for the call today — good to learn more about FinPay's planned rollout and the tight latency/throughput constraints for your fraud-scoring pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the engineering teams: 

- Scope: production inference for real-time scoring (200–500 qps peak), embeddings for similarity search, and a small reranking model for top-K results.
- Security requirements you called out: private connectivity from your VPC to Redwood, IP allowlist for control-plane APIs, egress restrictions (only a handful of IPs), DNS resolution for our endpoints, and mTLS preferred for control-plane + metrics ingestion.
- Integration asks from our side: we'll provide an SDK quickstart, examples for auth headers/token rotation, and a sample routing config for model variants + fallbacks. For embeddings/rerankers we'll include best-practice batching and a demo of structured output/tool-calling for enrichment.

Next steps
1) I'll loop in our network/infra lead (Jonas) and solutions engineer (Marissa) so we can share a concrete checklist and required IP ranges.
2) Please share the preferred date/time for a follow-up with your network/security folks (we recommend a 30–45 minute technical session).
3) I'll attach the VPC integration guide and a short networking checklist for your team to review.

Hi Mike / James —

Thanks for the details. Quick technical answers and a proposed checklist below. Attaching the full integration guide and a one-page networking checklist referenced earlier.

Short answers
- Control-plane IPs: We publish a small set of stable egress IPs per region for control-plane APIs and webhooks. For US region we currently publish three /28s; for firewall allowlisting we can provide the full list and add it to a static S3/Drive file that you can consume.
- VPC endpoints / Private DNS: Redwood supports three options depending on customer preference:
  1) Public endpoints + IP allowlist (simplest): your egress can NAT and resolve public DNS, then restrict by our published control-plane IPs.
  2) AWS PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint: we can publish an interface endpoint (customers create an endpoint in their VPC) — this avoids public egress and lets you keep DNS internal.
  3) Hybrid: use a PrivateLink for control-plane and public inference endpoints for lower-latency GPU pools.
- DNS & Egress: If you want internal DNS resolution we recommend the PrivateLink + private hosted zone approach. If you use NAT + public DNS, ensure your egress allows the three control-plane IP ranges and port 443.
- mTLS: We support mTLS for control-plane and metrics ingestion. For inference data plane we currently recommend mutual TLS for dedicated/private deployments; for hosted API token-based TLS (bearer tokens) is standard. If you need mTLS across the board we can generate a mutual-cert flow and integrate with your CA (or use our managed certs) — requires a short cert-exchange step during onboarding.

SDK / Auth notes
- SDK: Our SDKs (Python/Go/Node) default to bearer token auth in the Authorization header. They support automatic token rotation via a refresh endpoint and integrate with KMS for private deployments.
- Routing & structured output: You can pin model versions or use policy-based routing (latency/cost tier). For tool/structured output calling we recommend the SDK's structured_response utilities which include a small JSON schema wrapper and content-type negotiation. That doesn't require extra network ports beyond HTTPS.
- Embeddings & rerankers: Embedding requests are standard HTTPS calls; for high throughput we recommend batching (we provide a batching library in the SDK). Reranker flows often involve a local pre-filter + server-side rerank. Both require outbound HTTPS to the inference endpoints and do not need additional ports.

Proposed Integration Checklist (short)
1) Confirm desired connectivity mode: Public+allowlist OR PrivateLink.
2) If Public+allowlist: we'll provide the control-plane IP list and a sample firewall rule set.
3) If PrivateLink: share your AWS account ID and VPC/subnet details; we'll provide the endpoint service name and instructions to create the interface endpoint and private hosted zone.
4) Token auth: we'll provision a service account and initial API token; for Private deployments we can wire KMS-backed secrets.
5) mTLS (optional/if requested): exchange CA certs and commit to an mTLS test endpoint.
6) SDK quickstart: Marissa will share a repo with examples for auth header usage, batching for embeddings, and structured_output examples for tool-calling and rerank flows.
7) Test plan: smoke test (connectivity + auth), sample inference calls (gen, embeddings, rerank), performance test at 100 qps, then ramp to peak.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_integration_guide.pdf, networking-checklist.xlsx

Let me know which follow-up window works and we'll schedule the technical deep-dive (Jonas + Marissa + your network/security engineer).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
